title: Close the hole
briefing: shared.txt is world-writable (mode 666). Anyone could rewrite it. That's a security hole.
Take write away from 'others' — leave everyone able to read it.
tips: Symbolic chmod: `chmod o-w file` removes write for others without touching the rest.
objective: Remove write permission for 'others' from ~/shared.txt (group and owner keep what they have).
hints: You only want to change one bit: others' write. Symbolic chmod is surgical.
explanation: World-writable files let anyone tamper with them — a classic vulnerability. `chmod o-w` removes just others' write. Symbolic mode (u/g/o with +/-/= and r/w/x) changes one thing without disturbing the rest.
